findings.obligation: P1 and the locked no-secret promise the S1 rows restate ('the page hands no secret back to her', 'shows no secret anywhere'), and KPI-IIS-G1: no key or secret appears in any page, page source, log line, activity line, or in plaintext storage - on the replace path as on the first entry.
findings.observation: The rotation scenario asserts 'the page shows no key and no Slack secret', but the swept population planted() omits ROTATED_SIGNING_SECRET ('0f1e2d3c4b5a69788796a5b4c3d2e1f0'), the only secret this slice newly introduces: grep finds that constant only at its declaration (line 94), in Signer::secret (line 320) and in given_rotated_signing_secret (line 931). An implementation that re-rendered the just-submitted signing secret into the pre-filled replace form, or wrote it to a page the sweep reads, passes every S1 observation - the refusal path pins the two secret fields empty, but no observation on a successful rotation does. The KPI-IIS-G1 whole-sweep scenario (feature line 500) never rotates, so the database/log face of the same promise is unobserved for that value too. The oracle therefore records an observation it does not actually make for the value at risk.
findings.remediation: Add ROTATED_SIGNING_SECRET to planted()'s value list so every existing page, source, log, activity and plaintext-storage sweep covers it, and give the successful rotation a direct reading that the replace form hands back no secret (reuse then_form_kept after the save, which already pins both secret fields empty). Extend the KPI-IIS-G1 scenario's Given with 'Priya has rotated the Slack app's signing secret' so the rotated value is also searched in the database dump and the log lines. No new scenario is needed beyond that Given.

observations.text: Evidence basis: HEAD 16d1976, working tree clean (git status --porcelain empty), so the oracle and support bytes reviewed are the same bytes the acceptance designer's RED run consumed. Mechanical selection of oracle/support files changed since the slice base: argv 'git diff --name-only 7ccbc1b 16d1976 -- crates/' exit 0, stdout = crates/foundry-acceptance/src/steps/feature_instance_integration_setup.rs, crates/foundry-acceptance/src/support/instance_integration_setup.rs, crates/foundry-acceptance/tests/features/instance-integration-setup.feature (stderr empty). crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/slack_app.rs is unchanged at this commit, so the S1 row naming its field-shape table and generated field cases is existing coverage, not a new test. No lane re-execution: inputs (oracle, supports, production source, runtime) are byte-identical to the designer's run at this same revision, so that run is reused rather than restamped.

Measured RED (reused, original run by the acceptance designer in the shared Lima VM at this revision, full output /Users/jeffbailey/.cache/nwdes/iis-slack-replace-remove/s1-red.txt): argv 'scripts/test-in-lima.sh bash -c source scripts/eip-lanes.sh; eip_warm; eip_lane us-iis-05', exit 101; 1 feature, 9 scenarios (9 failed), 80 steps (71 passed, 9 failed), 0 parsing errors, 0 hook errors. Every failure is semantic, not infrastructure: each failing step is a driving-port step (save_slack_app, then_form_kept, given_rotated_signing_secret) whose panic names the missing business behaviour ('Priya finds the Slack app form on the instance integrations page ... with no form there she cannot paste a regenerated secret'), and the captured page body shows /admin/instance/integrations answering 200 OK with the saved-app section and no Slack form. All 71 preceding steps (Background, key, secrets key, first Slack save, replica offers) pass, so no import error, missing fixture or path mismatch is masquerading as RED.

Obligation closure, P1: E1/E2 the replace form over a saved app in effect is read through the real page (then_form_kept asserts the pre-filled client ID and both secret fields empty); E3 no confirm step is falsified by then_on_instance_page, which requires the answer path to be /admin/instance/integrations and a success status right after the POST; E4 'every replica within 60 seconds' is a whole-population observation - then_every_replica_verifies asks each replica at its own address (replica_addrs) and the 60 s bound is read for the whole observation (both waited and wall.elapsed against LIVE_BOUND), so the replica that took the change cannot answer for the other; E5 the exact I-x sentence is read; the kept client secret is falsifiable because the Slack double accepts only the exact client secret the app was saved with (slack_double.rs:712-713, armed with the feature's CLIENT_SECRET at instance_integration_setup.rs:467), so a blank field that cleared or overwrote it makes the code exchange fail. The replaced signing secret is observed refused as unauthorised, and the rotated one accepted, in separate scenarios, so neither an accept-everything nor a refuse-everything implementation passes.

Obligation closure, P2 and P6: the refusal outline drives the real POST with a different client ID and one blank secret in each run, reads the exact I-11 sentence with the field named, asserts the form hands the typed client ID back with both secret fields empty, and then_saved_app_unchanged observes the preserved universe on four viewers - the page still names the app with both secrets set, the Activity list records no replacement, Add to Slack still asks Slack approval for that client ID, and an event signed with the secret the app was saved with still verifies - so a half-applied submission cannot pass. The takeover scenario observes the new app both on the page and at Slack's approval redirect. P6's 'replaced' line is observed as a whole population: then_activity_lines assert_eq's the entire Activity list, newest first, against the three expected lines, so wrong words ('saved the Slack app', a raw 'slack app replaced' fallback), a missing line or a duplicated line all fail. P6's 'removed' arm (expectation E23) has no observation in S1, which matches S1's scope (rotate or replace only; Remove is a later slice) and remains an open feature completion obligation.

Defect evidence, the secrecy sweep's population: the rotation scenario ends with the step 'the page shows no key and no Slack secret', which is then_page_shows_nothing_secret sweeping the page body and the redirect location for every value returned by planted(). planted() (crates/foundry-acceptance/src/support/instance_integration_setup.rs:1823-1830) lists OPERATOR_KEY, OTHER_OPERATOR_KEY, LEGACY_KEY, CLIENT_SECRET, SIGNING_SECRET, OTHER_CLIENT_SECRET, OTHER_SIGNING_SECRET, the held instance key, the generated secrets key and the double's issued tokens. ROTATED_SIGNING_SECRET ('0f1e2d3c4b5a69788796a5b4c3d2e1f0') appears only at its declaration (line 94), in Signer::secret (line 320) and in given_rotated_signing_secret (line 931): grep shows no other use, so it is in no swept population, on the page or in the database dump used by the KPI-IIS-G1 scenario at feature line 500 (whose Given sequence never rotates). The value the slice newly introduces is therefore the one value no secrecy observation looks for.

diagnostic: S1's oracle is public, constructible and independent, and its RED is semantic on all nine scenarios (exit 101, 9/9 failed, 0 parsing/hook errors, every panic naming the missing replace form through a driving-port step). P1 and P2 close: the pre-filled form, the blank field that keeps the saved client secret (falsifiable because the Slack double accepts only the exact saved client secret), no confirm step, the per-replica 60-second observation asked at each replica's own address, the replaced secret refused and the rotated one accepted in separate scenarios, the I-11 refusal with the whole saved universe preserved on four viewers, and the I-18 'replaced' line read as the entire Activity list. One concrete defect blocks approval: the secrecy sweep's population excludes ROTATED_SIGNING_SECRET, the only secret the slice introduces, so a page that echoed the just-submitted signing secret back into the replace form would pass every S1 observation while the oracle claims to have looked (owner oracle, one-line population fix plus one Given on the KPI-IIS-G1 scenario). Re-review is limited to that correction and the no-secret obligation. Non-blocking and retained: P6's 'removed' arm (E23) is out of S1's scope and stays a feature completion obligation; the replaced secret is observed refused only on the single-process Foundry, judged covered by composition; typesafe: unavailable (jev_decide.py exit 3, TYPESAFE_API_KEY absent), both oracle-critique questions answered locally from the bytes.
